tips.comment: Has several positive factors. The slow going, the booking of Rossa Ryan, who rode a winner for this yard yesterday, has won over the distance and ran a good second last time out.
Crack Shot went off favourite last time and is obviously well thought of by this yard. The booking of David Egan is a plus and dropping into this class could prove the key to getting a win

MR KING appeared to shape with more promise than the bare figures suggest at York last time out. He could now be coming to hand for northern trainer Iain Jardine and this race has less depth than his latest contest. One of the more likely types.
No comment made

Kept on well after leading Lto, when coming 2/7 beaten a length in a similar class handicap over 7f @ Leicester. Goes off same mark here, step back up to a mile a plus, has form @ higher level, under used jockey retains ride and very good trainer best here with his 4yo plus @ 25 percent last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Race 6 at Carlisle today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,566 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding Look Back Smiling from the Gemma Tutty yard. It will be ridden by Connor Beasley. This son of Fast Company is a five-time winner, is distance suited, and will have no problem with the going. It has as good a chance as any in this wide-open looking race today.

It's an open looking race, wouldn't be a surprise to see horses at big odds running well. This selection has some good form in the book in some good races, if he can get back to that level he'll be running well. Looks fairly well treated, small each-way tip.

Urban Sprawl has been consistent of late and gets a apprentice up today in Archie Young who negates 5lb here..the form from its last runs bodes well has that has been franked..extra places here too so looks a player ew

Won his last three starts off a busy three year old campaign and made a promising return to action at Musselburgh in April over an extended 7f. Did well to finish a close up 3rd having had anything but the smoothest of passages during the race. Not in the same form back there just 6 days later but wasn’t suited by the way the race was run, having been slowly away. Can hopefully get back on track here racing off the same mark over a slightly longer trip.

A left field swing at the Carlisle Bell, with Sailthisshipalone entitled to improve for the run last time. It’s an effort that, in the face of it, gives him loads to find with the favorite, but he finds himself down in class and at the bottom of the weights with Fentiman's 5lbs claim taking him clear. His second run last season was a seasonal best effort in a competitive York handicap, and he runs off a career-low mark now. His best efforts have come on GS/S, so that’s a bonus. Best efforts have come over shorter, so he should appreciate an overall lack of pace, and he tops the speed ratings of these as well. His sole victory came from 2 runs in this class.

Hiromichi is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Jack Channon. He is 8/29 wins, so has been prolific for connections??'a dream horse. He has won five times over today's mile and twice on good to soft ground and won't mind any further rain, having won on soft at Ripon on his last win off 82 and runs today off 81. So, he also looks handily weighted for a trainer who has found his mojo with 9/20 wins in recent weeks. He makes his third track appearance today after a 289-day break, and his last two wins have come on the third start after a 62-153 day break. So, Hiromichi may be coming to hand, and at 25-1 under Clifford Lee, this grand old gelding is of interest.

What has happened to Navagio? The James Horton-trained 6yo Footstepsinthesand gelding was 3rd in the C2 Lincoln Handicap off a mark of 96 at Donny on soft ground in March last year. That was his last bit of form, and he has been out of form since. It takes a leap of faith to back him today. However, if he can recapture some of his old form in this Cl4 handicap off a reduced mark of 82 and on his favourite ground, he might nick one of the 5 places. He is a hold-up merchant and, in my opinion, has a decent draw in 17, with the main pace likely to come from 16 and 10.

Redarna might be getting on a bit but did win in a C4 before the break in October off today's mark. Returned for a couple of runs in C2 and C3 last month and is another that the return to C4 might see a revival. EW 5P.
None from eight over this trip, but did win going away last time out like a horse who has a bit more to offer off present mark and has won here. Bit chance to complete the hat trick.

The Ed Bethell trained Orangesandlemons has been a model of consistency with her career form which eeads 22-2212. The 3yo Mayson filly is certainly open to improvement on a mark of 75 with 7f probably her optimum trip. I think she is more than capable of a big run in an open race and so say the bells of St Clement's.
Blufferonthebus last won off a 67 and tends to go well here, including one of two seconds this month, only missing out by half a length. Worth another shot while still on a 64.

She suffered from seconditis last summer when she finished runner-up in 3 consecutive runs. Much improved effort LTO when a useful 2 of 10 at Chester last month. I think she can be a threat off the current dropped mark.

Beronia returns from a 53 day break. She disappointed on her last run at Newmarket but had placed 2nd at Doncaster in her prior race. That was over six furlongs so the drop in trip should suit her and puts her into the frame.
Remains a maiden after seven starts but ran a cracker to finish runner-up over course and distance last time, and a repeat of that form would see her go close today.
No comment made
Soul Dance won very easily at Nottingham 3 weeks ago. Has gone up a big 10lb for that win, but it looked as if there was more to come. Has a good chance.

With 3 places on offer, this has to be backed each way on handicap debut and with Levey booked for the ride. Beaten only by a pattern class filly on debut last September. Much better than a 72-rated handicapper.

INVINCIBLE DUKE drops in class and has a talented 7lb claiming appfentice aboard. These factors can help his cause and his last two effort against officially stronger rivals have been creditable. Against his own age group he appeals.

She can do much better than what was on show LTO when 9 of 14 at Newbury earlier this month. But now with a dropped mark and only 1lb higher than her last winning mark, I think she can bounce back strongly.
Cape Breton will be suited by this increase in trip and should be able to do well in this company. Fantastic chance to get off the mark.

Tremorgio makes a handicap debut for trainer Charlie Appleby. Won on turf last year in this class (3). Ran in a class 2 novice last time out on the all-weather. Going to have quicker ground today but looks like a decent type who shouldn't be far away.
Disappointed last time but enters handicap company on what looks like a low mark. Cheekpieces are on today, and a big run can be expected.

Super impressed with the finishing effort when scoring over C&D last time and I think a 6lb rise is extremely lenient. You may get bigger on the exchanges, as the books don't want to push their prices out.

Course and distance winner around this time last year. Changed stables just after that and made a winning reappearance for his new yard. He then finished second to a horse I put up on here who looked a good bet. Freshened up by a six-week break, I fancy him to bounce back here and go close.
This five-year-old won really well at Huntingdon LTO, and that form has since been boosted. A three-pound rise in the weights looks more than manageable.

A trappy-looking weak race here. Just Chasing May is trained by Ben Pauling and ridden by Ben Jones, and has run 14 times with a win rate of 7.1% and a place rate of 35.7%. He was in good form through last autumn before disappointing when too keen over 3m at Southwell in January, so the return to shorter could suit here. His current mark of 94 is workable to me, given past placed efforts in similar races, and he goes fine on good ground. Off 142 days, which might leave him needing it slightly, but he has run well fresh before. Each way chance if settling better early and there is a good pace to aim at.
No comment made

Mr Yeats has had three starts for this yard since joining, all in Class 4. Fell first time, then came 4th at Warwick, where he seemed to be re-educated. Was kept in rear on latest start 12 days ago before staying on for 4th. He is now below his last winning mark and dropped in grade today. Looks sure to be asked serious questions by his rider. If he responds, he has the ability to win.

Not sure what went wrong when tailing off @ Stratford Lto, but won this race last year off a 3lb lower mark and drop back to this 2.4 miles will suit better. Very under used jockey back up and shrewd trainer best here with his hurdlers last 5 seasons @ 13 percent, making current 16/1 decent Ew value in the race.

The model I run suggests Boskill Borden can win this one. Boskill Borden lines up here with the highest RPR of the larger 15 runner field and has an official ranking that is the second lowest. This subsequently means Boskill Borden goes out with the second lowest weight to carry around this 2m 4f trip. Shane Fenelon takes off a further 3 lbs claiming. Boskill Borden tries the visor for the first time to aid concentration. Form figures show some ability with 4th and 5th place finishes but the addition of the visor might give the improvement required. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Outback Frontiers won in July last year off 79. He was raised 4lb for that and went chasing over the winter with no success. He has had no prep for this which is a concern but he has a favourable weight so, if fit enough, he has an EW chance.

Dubai Beach has already had two quick wins this month. Although up ten pounds under a penalty for her two wins, she won easily by five and a half lengths last time at Chelmsford. The handicapper is due to add another nine pounds.

My selection was absolutely abysmal on the latest run, but Stateira has only had 3 races, winning first time up at Southwell when totally unfancied (28/1). The second run was a third place over C&D. I'll forgive the last run as a blip, as there is value in the price if

Both wins to date have been on AW, so will welcome a return back to AW, especially after a poor run at Chester LTO when only 11 of 12 this month. Dropped mark and drop down in class just might prove to be the difference.

Flagon Dry won a C5 when last out in December and has since changed yards. It's worth a chance that the new yard has him ready for this return in C4, which puts him well-weighted among today's runners. EW 4P.

Just four career runs for the 3yo filly and still room for improvement. She has been beaten 2L in each of her races. Nothing went right on her handicap debut three weeks ago but she stayed on well late on, just a nk behind the runner-up and the race was won by a consistent and decent yardstick. Could be worth another chance.

Maids Head is in stall number 3, which is a handy draw for a filly who likes to settle midfield. She is trained by Marco Botti and ridden by Robert Havlin, and has had 9 runs with a win rate of 11.11% and a place rate of 66.67%. Got back on track when stepping up in trip to score narrowly off 67 at Chelmsford and now runs off 70. Consistent with form figures of 32641 in handicaps, handles this surface, and has placed on similar ground. Up in class, but I reckon she can go close again. Each way chance with a good pace to aim at today.
Stella Hogan has shown some promise in recent runs and returns now to Kempton, where she has strong form figures. Jason Watson gets a solid tune out here, and this can go well.
Marchetti returned after a five-month break to Chepstow, placing 5th out of 12. She was not that far off in this race and could be one to consider if building on that race.

Chadleeny was underwhelming as a 2-year-old, but I think this one's got a lot of potential. Ed Walker's horses are running really well at the minute as well. Drawn wider than ideal, but there's been plenty of winners out of draw 11 overall. Conditions shouldn't be a problem. It's all on how well the horse has been working at home. I'm hoping this one gives us a run for the money at a nice price.
Beautifully bred and cost 280k as a yearling. Sure-fire improver after his debut last time, shaping well despite being too keen. Should win here.
Finished in midfield on his racecourse debut over 6f at Leicester. Shaped as though further would suit ideally but is kept to that trip here, switched to the AW and is no forlorn hope.
No comment made

With 1 win from 3 races this year, he is showing promise. His best performance to date was a victory in a 6 runner handicap at this C&D just 14 days ago. Despite being nudged up 2lb, the 4-year-old is expected to be competitive, especially with the skilled John Egan riding.

Letmebetheboss is in stall number 5, which is fine for a stayer over this trip. He is trained by William Muir and Chris Grassick and ridden by Lewis Edmunds. He has run 14 times with a win rate of 7.1% and a place rate of 35.7%. He produced a clear career best when bursting forward 3 lengths clear over 1m6f at Southwell last time off a mark of 52. He now goes up in trip and up 6lb to a mark of 58. First try on Polytrack, but bred to stay and see it out well. If backing up that last run, he holds strong win claims in a race lacking depth, and the pace should suit him here.

Won at Southwell in February off a mark three pounds lower than this and looks well in today. Not sure Wolverhampton suited last time, and this track should be much more to his liking. The yard has had two winners from only ten runners in the last two weeks. Hollie Doyle is a great booking, and she has six winners over the same time period.

Race 8 at Kempton today is a Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,217 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding, The Colorist, from the Karen Jewell yard, and will be ridden by Robert Havlin. This son of Time Test has been knocking on the door for his next win, and a line can surely be drawn through his latest when pulled up in running. On form, he has a top chance today.

Innisfree Pearl had the speed to win on the sharp track at Brighton in September. The filly kept on well over the 12 furlongs trip. As a daughter of the great stayer Yeats it doesn't take much to imagine her being even better stepping up to two miles on this flat track.

Three career runs for the 3-year-old. Last time out on turf. Better judged on her first two starts, both at this track, a strong-looking novice stakes and maiden stakes. No answer towards the finish in those races but not disgraced. An opening handicap mark of 60 in this low-grade contest is tempting. Good jockey booking for this apprentice riders’ handicap.

Was a well beaten fourth when dropped back to 1m at Ripon at the end of last month but wasn't beaten far when finishing second when dropped back to today's trip at Yarmouth a fortnight ago. Has won one and placed in two of her last four starts. Sam Garcia's 7lb claim should come in useful. Should be thereabouts.

Unknown Journey is in stall number 3, which is decent but not ideal for a strong pace. Trained by Amanda W Carroll and ridden by Matthew Slater, he has run 19 times with a 15.79% win rate and a 31.58% place rate. Last time, he was below form, dropping sharply in trip and finishing fourth, beaten 5 and a quarter lengths at Goodwood over 7f. This shorter trip does look a bit on the sharp side for him, and he may prefer further, but he does handle the polytrack well, so giving him a chance here today.
If backing up the effort when last seen, Lunar Orbit should really be doing a lot better than the odds suggest here. Has a winning chance and will go off shorter, I think.

Three runs for the 3-year-old this year. Two respectable runs, then finding his feet three weeks ago when beaten just a short head after a poor passage, but still well clear of the rest. The winner rated much higher than what he now faces in this handicap.

Was well beaten over 7f here last month but wasn't beaten far when finishing fourth from eight over the same trip at Yarmouth a fortnight later. Is a two time course winner over 7f. Step up in trip should suit. Should be involved at the finish.
Possibly had issues as only seen twice since a promising debut last November. Shaped well on reappearance in April, but not seen since. Worth an each-way punt.

Twelve races have passed since his last victory in 2024. Recently, the gelding performed below expectations, finishing 7th in a C&D handicap 28 days ago, having made his move earlier than preferred. However, the trainer is currently in excellent form, and with Richard Kingscote on board, if he can bring this distance winner up to pace, an each-way bet at 16/1 could yield a profit.
Atlantic Gamble has won six races from 1 mile to 1 mile 1 furlong, including 4 wins on the all-weather. Earlier this month, finished 5th over 1 mile in Chelmsford City.

Stellenbosch is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Richard Hannon. He is 0-5 wins and has only made one appearance in a handicap under Sean Levey off a mark of 80, leading for much of the way only to weaken in the latter part of the race. So, he is unexposed in this sphere and makes a second appearance in a handicap off an 8lb lower mark on 72, with the kind handicapper dropping him 5lb and Alec Voikhansky 3lb. A change in handicap mark could bring about a change in fortune. He comes here in half-decent nick, leading again and just got outpointed by 1/2l when finishing 3/12 at Chelmsford in a maiden. Outside chance.
Early days, but I do think he has some potential and looks to be more of a threat on AW. Probably a fair starting mark in handicap debut, and course experience should help.
Rajak made two runs over six furlongs at Chelmsford City this month. He was not totally disgraced, and the runs suggest that the extra furlong will help and suit him to get closer this time.
Maiden, who was a good 4th in a Windsor maiden at a huge 100/1 last time. A repeat of that gives this one an each-way squeak.

C&D victor. Placed 9th in a handicap at Goodwood 33 days prior. With the weights in her favour and both the trainer and jockey in excellent form, she has a solid chance to bounce back from her last outing.

Just seven runs for the 4yo. Three runs this year. He didn’t really fire on turf last time out, but he has better stats on the AW and comes here fresh after a six-week break. Only beaten a shd in a 14-runner handicap on his previous start on this polytrack surface, the rest coming home in single file, the winner rated much higher than the rivals he now faces.

Xiomara had a good season last year for the previous handler. Although the last two starts in French Listed events were below par, both came on heavy going. She had two runs at Windsor on quick ground for new connections. Neither race went to plan, but she could get her season going with the switch to this track, as her sire has a good record over this course and distance.

Crystal Mariner is in stall number 13, which is not ideal and may force him wide into the first turn on this track. He is trained by Jamie Osborne and ridden by Saffie Osborne, and has run 13 times with no wins and a place rate of 23.1%. He ran well at Lingfield two starts ago and is better judged on that effort than his latest run at Windsor when beaten 8 lengths. Polytrack suits him better, and the return to 10f helps here, and the tongue strap remains on. Still a maiden but has shaped like a winner-in-waiting at this level. Each way chance if settling early and pace is fair.
This gelding looks value to me. Hollie rides and she was aboard for his last win. He's only a pound higher tonight. The yard are in decent form too.
At the right end of weights with a good draw. Just 4th handicap start and was a 3L 7th here LTO in a competitive class 3 handicap. Down in grade here from same mark.

Gelded son of Postponed & Tigerfish ( Dam's sire Lilbourne Lad ) who was last seen at Chelmsford 24 days ago where finishing 10th/12 however that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 207 day break and he is most certainly entitled to strip fitter with that run under his belt drops back down in trip racing at the 1 mile 2 furlong 219 yards trip that being a positive move by his connections and he can be shown to best effect over this trip especially arriving here in a much fitter state this time out currently operating on a mark of 76 W Stone's inmate looks poised for a big run here and he should have plenty more to offer now as a 4yo handily drawn coming out of gate 1 here at Kempton Tipsy Tiger can make his presence strongly felt in a race that should also be run to suit his nature of going very well given the horses enrolled to run here jockey Brandon Wilkie takes off a handy 3lb which can only help his cause here

Has the highest mark in this field and switches back to flats after an encouraging effort over jumps at Fontwell LTO last December. If he can overcome rustiness, I do think he can be a serious threat. He won here last November over a much higher mark and longer distance, so in this context, I think he is overpriced.

This is going to be my second last tip on OLBG. I can't compete with those that have an average of 200 tips a month and get lucky now and again. Fancy Dancer ran well the other day against the well-ridden White Umbrella. As long as the firm ground doesn't affect her, then she should win tomorrow.

Rogue Endeavour is in stall number 2, which is a good draw for a front or close midfield run. Trained by George Harris and ridden by Ray Dawson, he has run 27 times with a win rate of 11% and a place rate of 26%. Below form last time, beaten 8 lengths at Lingfield, and the current handicap mark of 51 is low and sliding lower. But he needs to be having a good day to get his backside moving. An each-way chance if things click and he is in the 'mood' and the pace is strong.

Was well beaten on his first three starts back following seven months off in March but improved to win comfortably over C&D last month and wasn't beaten far when finishing third when dropped back to 5f at Nottingham five days later before being well beaten over the same trip at Wetherby three weeks ago. Was gelded during the break. Yard in good form recently. Elizabeth Gale in good form recently and her 7lb claim should come in useful. Should be thereabouts.

Offiahs Boy thrives on fast ground, as evidenced by his 16.67% win rate on similar going. His class record is strong, with a win and two places from six runs, and his current handicap mark of 51 is workable.
Always in the mix and can't be underestimated, going off the same mark as last time. His second at Brighton at the beginning of this month sets a very good standard to aim at.

Love Is The Law's recent Lingfield performance, beaten only 3l off a 74 handicap, indicates she’s competitive at this mark. With a 50% record in this class, including two wins, she’s proven at this level.

Highly promising gelded son of Dark Angel & Samira Gold ( Dam's sire Gold Away ) who was last seen at Lingfield 25 days ago where finishing 6th/11 however he shaped much better than that bare result suggests as he wasn't ideally placed on the occasion and once he tried to get on terms to mount his challenge he was unluckily denied a clear run at a crucial stage of the race resulting in him unable to make a serious impact however Dr R Newland & J Insole's inmate has really been on the upgrade recently and he remains with all potential in tact and has found an excellent opportunity to make it win number 3 this year currently operating on unchanged mark of 75 which is well within range Knights Gold looks poised to bounce back here jockey Elizabeth Gale takes off a very valuable looking 7lb which only enhances his good looking claims here bold showing is anticipated . Respected .
Makes a decent journey here in search of a four-timer, and with not much form in today's opposition, looks a strong chance to justify his odds.

Thank The Lord has worn a visor successfully in five wins and he handles similar going well. With a solid 22.73% win rate in this class, a favorable handicap, and a capable jockey in L Morris, he’s poised for success.
Last of her 5 wins came at Chepstow in September. Has finished in the frame on all 4 outings at the Wesh venue this season and is still on last winning mark.

C&D and course winner Sisters In The Sky hasn't been too far away in his busy schedule at Bath recently, and his mark has dropped an enticing 4 lbs to 50. Ray Dawson has been in good form recently with seven winners and eleven places from his last forty rides.

Gained first win in competitive Brighton handicap last time, and this lightly raced four-year-old can go in again. Up two pounds for that but still sixteen pounds below the initial mark. The trainer has had two winners in the last two weeks and does well in these types of races. Callum Shepherd is a good booking, and he also has a couple of recent winners.

Low key start to the season, but with excuses. Drops down to a handy mark and has a great record over course and distance, especially at this level of competition. Won a similar contest under this claimer last summer and looks good value at double digits.
Bring It On has been twice placed in strong novice fields, handles firm ground well, and drops in trip. Solid claims with early speed. He's a definite player in this lineup.
6th in course and distance maiden last time out. Only needs to find some small improvement to win this today.

Jockey had some big wins in 2-year-old events over the past 2 seasons, shows £108 LSP. This season shows a 27% win rate. At these odds, in a 5f event, and with a horse that tends to lead, could well surprise here.
Step up in trip sure to be in his favor and likely to be a lot of improvement. Should be difficult to beat here.

Galactic Glow has a proven 30% win rate at this course and distance, with three victories from ten runs. His recent Chepstow performance, narrowly beaten by a quarter-length off a 47 handicap, shows he’s in top form.
Better than bare result over course and distance last time. Finished 4th having met trouble in running and made to switch. Comes here off same mark.

Split Silk is in stall number 3, which is a fair draw for dropping in and settling early. She is trained by Ollie Sangster and ridden by S D Bowen, and has run 8 times with no wins or places. Giving her another go today. Last time out, she pulled far too hard and failed to stay when down the field at Leicester over 10f. Now wears blinkers for the first time, which might help her settle. Dropping in trip could suit her breeding pedigree, and she runs off a basement mark of 50, which gives me something to work with. If the headgear sparks improvement, she could outrun her odds today, and the draw and trip could help her also.

Backing Villalobos, the experienced 6-year-old Footstepsinthesand gelding trained by Simon Hodgson, in tonight’s Secured Alarm Systems Handicap over 1m 2f at Bath. He arrives on the back of a strong reappearance run at this course 18 days ago, finishing a solid second over this trip on good ground, after dropping down in class??'an effort that saw him emerge as the main danger in form terms. Despite that, he was a distance behind the one he chased, but conditions and trip are right in his wheelhouse. Rated on around 52 with an RPR of 60, and carrying just 9st 12lb, he looks well treated for this level in a small field of 6 runners, where his experience around Bath??'where he has a win in the book in the autumn??'could prove decisive. He showed last time he handles the course and copes with the trip, and tonight’s contest appears tailor-made to suit him.
Only just beaten at Cork and on an upward trajectory form-wise. Showed improvement at Ascot in a tough field. Back up in trip, can only see her going one better here and likes the going today.

Havana Anna has some half decent form in the book and will be hard to beat if managing further improvement but the beautifully bred Dawn Romance looks better value. She's from a yard who can certainly ready one and Colin Keane is booked to guide her through her debut.

Risky tip, the good odds are the main reason for me placing this tip. Horses 4 and 2 are the better options but Mini Cotai might do a bit better on today's better ground conditions, struggled on the very testing conditions last time out, had run better on debut which was on better ground conditions. Still has time for improvement, progress definitely needed though.

Having shown a performance reminiscent of her debut, this Frankel filly finished a reasonable 3rd in a maiden at this C&D 38 days ago, although she did tire towards the end. If she can achieve a similar effort, she is likely to be in the mix again.
Great chance in this maiden race. The horse has some nice pedigree and looks to have the ground and trip to suit today.

Looked a doubtful stayer last time out but might well have need the race after 200+ days out and shrewd yard stick with same distance today. Perhaps worth another chance then with Colin Keane to assist.

Just the two starts so far and improved on her debut effort when finishing 5th over an extended 7f at Leopardstown last time. Was keeping on steadily in the straight having been slightly hampered turning in. More to come and worth a second look.

This is a risky tip, the odds reflect that so it's just a small each-way risky tip because of the good odds. Finished last on that last run but did travel quite well for most of the way and faded late on, may be wiser for that experience and this slight drop in trip may be more suitable.
Short enough in the betting, but does look a progressive sort from the Ger Lyons stable. Won both starts to date, and there could be more to come now stepping up in trip.
Won the Kooyonga Stakes (Listed) - solid profile and always looks impressive. Harrington and Foley are a major combo not to be overlooked today. Strong finisher and peaking in form.
Just failed at Gowran last time out. She has her trip tonight and represents a yard with a fine record in this race. Looks excellent ew value at 7's.
Dawn Spirit placed last at Leopardstown three weeks ago. She did not have the stamina for the extra two furlongs, and the drop in trip should help her to squeeze into the frame.

Shaped promisingly on his debut in a mile maiden at Gowran and was doing his best work late on. The way he finished then, and again at Killarney last time when beaten in a photo finish, suggests that ideally further than this would suit. He still rates as a serious player.

Second on debut over 7f where the form has been boosted since, and then ran third over 10f, looking that trip a bit too far. Back over a mile here should suit better and may have enough progress coming to overturn the odds-on favorite.
A modest enough 4th at Gowran on debut but should improve on that here and if so has definite each way possibilities at the very least.

This Once-raced gelding came in 14th in a maiden at Limerick on his debut 14 days ago. The Slattery yard is in good shape, and this 3 year old might deserve another opportunity at enticing odds of 100/1. An each-way wager appears to be a sensible option with a senior jockey taking the reins.
Missed break on debut but was staying on at the finish. Will come on for that run, and if getting away better, can make the frame. Cheekpieces fitted for the first time could help.
Paddydaddy ran and finished 2nd at the weekend, runs again here, quickly after that run. He was hampered towards the end in that race and has a good chance of winning here.
Left maiden form well behind on handicap debut last time out when beaten under two lengths over this trip. Last time out, although up five pounds, looks the one to beat.
Now on a very good mark and has ran respectably of late making the frame on each of his last two starts. Not one to overly rely on but a good place prospect if near his best.

UNTERBERG may have found the right trip/ground on turf and he is fourth-up for this campaign with potential to peak. In this all apprentice riders race Wayne Hassett is an excellent experienced pilot and although yet to win in this sphere of racing there are a few things in his favour today.
Magnetic North ran on well on Monday to win at Ballinrobe by three and three-quarter lengths. Veteran is again ridden by the very useful apprentice Nicola Burns. Each way chance.
Pandion Power gets some headgear/hood on for the first time after going well enough in its last race, where the form took a wee boost recently. Johnny Murtagh in decent nick. ew

Ran twice as a two-year-old and, having shown something to work on when making his debut, failed to build on that on his final two-year-old start at Gowran, again over a mile. Apparently scoped badly after that race and had been gelded ahead of his return to action at Navan but was again below that debut form. May have needed that run but was only marginally better last time at Killarney. Starting out for a new yard now for handicap debut, he has a bit to prove but could reward each-way interest.

Could be some real value bet if she comes to the party like she did last year around this time. Still lightly raced but has struggled in her last few races. Yido Geerharey takes over with a five-pound claimer and is likely to improve with a falling mark.

This horse can't get much lower in the weights and should be able to do a lot better today over this extended 10f. The jockey is in some form, and the horse has shown good form at Naas before. Must be capable of winning off this mark and bottom weight at some time in the near future given his previous form off substantially higher marks.
Improving sort who went close in a good race last time. The winner that day has since gone and won again. Sets the standard on form.
Billy Lee is a notable jockey booking for connections and this horse certainly looks capable of winning this race without issues

The wide draw isn't ideal for this selection but can still be considered, it is possible to run well over this course and distance from this wide draw. Ran well in what was a good race last time out, today's race won't be much tougher. Wears first time Cheekpieces today which may bring about some improvement.
My Girl Sioux is frustrating to follow. She runs well but has managed so far only one win from 50 attempts, and that was last November. Nevertheless, she is expected to be thereabouts again.
A wide-open sprint handicap where American in Paris appeals at a big-looking 16/1. He ran well at Fairyhouse 11 days ago, and if repeating that run off of a reduced mark, he should go close.
They are dropping this one back down to 5f with the same jockey on board, and they are putting the first-time visor on this one. A good value each-way bet for the 4 places available.

With no course winners in this field, it looks about as open an event as you can get. But I'm drawn maybe by the jockey D P McDonogh on board Lismacbryan, which didn't run that bad on stable debut when not much room, not far in behind. Looks a massive price on that run?
